enhanced.fullText:
The Pennsylvania Sexual Violence Education Act, codified under 24 P.S. Section 5104, establishes comprehensive requirements for sexual violence prevention education in public schools throughout the Commonwealth. This regulation is designed to enhance student safety and wellness by providing age-appropriate education about sexual violence prevention, recognition, and response protocols.

All public school districts in Pennsylvania must implement sexual violence prevention education programs that align with state-approved curricula and evidence-based practices. The education must be developmentally appropriate and delivered by qualified instructors who have received specialized training in sexual violence prevention and trauma-informed approaches.

For elementary grades (K-5), instruction shall focus on body safety, appropriate versus inappropriate touch, personal boundaries, and trusted adult communication. Students must learn to identify safe adults and understand basic concepts of consent appropriate to their developmental level. Content must emphasize empowerment and personal safety without creating fear or anxiety.

Middle school programs (grades 6-8) shall expand upon foundational concepts to include more detailed discussions of personal boundaries, healthy relationships, peer pressure, digital citizenship related to sexual content, and bystander intervention strategies. Students must receive information about available resources and reporting mechanisms within the school and community.

High school curricula (grades 9-12) must provide comprehensive education covering consent, sexual assault prevention, dating violence, stalking, harassment, and the intersection of substance use and sexual violence. Programs shall address the impact of technology and social media on sexual violence, including non-consensual sharing of intimate images and online exploitation.

All programs must incorporate trauma-informed practices and recognize that students may have experienced sexual violence. Instructors must be prepared to respond appropriately to disclosures and connect students with appropriate resources. Content must be inclusive of all students regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, or disability status.

School districts must establish clear policies regarding parent/guardian notification about sexual violence education programs. Parents must receive advance notice of program content and have the opportunity to review materials. Districts must provide alternative educational activities for students whose parents exercise opt-out provisions while ensuring these students still receive essential safety information.

Districts shall collaborate with local sexual assault service providers, law enforcement agencies, and other community partners to enhance program effectiveness and ensure students have access to appropriate resources. Guest speakers and external program providers must be pre-approved and meet district standards for background clearances and training requirements.

Schools must maintain safe and supportive environments that encourage reporting of sexual violence incidents. Clear reporting protocols must be established, communicated to all students and staff, and regularly reviewed. All school personnel must receive annual training on recognizing signs of sexual violence, responding to disclosures, and fulfilling mandatory reporting obligations.

The regulation requires districts to collect and maintain data on program implementation, student participation rates, and outcomes measures where appropriate. This information must be reported annually to the Pennsylvania Department of Education and used for continuous program improvement.

Districts must ensure that sexual violence education is culturally responsive and addresses the unique needs of their student populations. Programs should acknowledge that certain communities may face higher risks of sexual violence and tailor prevention strategies accordingly.

Funding for program implementation may be available through state grants, federal funding streams, and partnerships with community organizations. Districts are encouraged to pursue collaborative funding approaches and resource sharing with neighboring districts.

Compliance monitoring will be conducted through regular review of district policies, curricula, and implementation practices. The Department of Education will provide technical assistance and professional development opportunities to support effective program implementation.

Violations of this regulation may result in corrective action plans, additional oversight requirements, or other sanctions as determined by the Department of Education. Districts must demonstrate good faith efforts to comply with all requirements and address any identified deficiencies promptly.

This regulation recognizes that sexual violence prevention is an ongoing process requiring sustained commitment from educators, families, and communities. Regular evaluation and updating of programs ensures they remain current with best practices and responsive to emerging challenges in student safety and wellness.
enhanced.summary: The Pennsylvania Sexual Violence Education Act requires all public school districts to implement age-appropriate sexual violence prevention education programs from grades K-12. Districts must use qualified instructors, trauma-informed approaches, and evidence-based curricula while maintaining parent notification requirements. Programs must address consent, healthy relationships, bystander intervention, and available resources. Schools must establish clear reporting protocols, collaborate with community partners, and maintain supportive environments that encourage disclosure of incidents.
requirements: Implement developmentally appropriate sexual violence prevention education for grades K-12 using state-approved, evidence-based curricula delivered by specially trained instructors
Establish clear parent/guardian notification procedures with advance notice of program content, material review opportunities, and opt-out provisions with alternative activities
Provide annual training for all school personnel on recognizing signs of sexual violence, responding to disclosures, and fulfilling mandatory reporting obligations
Collaborate with local sexual assault service providers, law enforcement, and community partners to enhance program effectiveness and student resource access
Maintain trauma-informed, inclusive programs that address the needs of all students regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, or disability status

reportingRequirements.timeline: Annual reporting to Pennsylvania Department of Education by June 30th each year, including program implementation data, student participation rates, staff training completion, community partnerships established, and outcome measures. Incident reports must be filed within 24 hours of disclosure with appropriate authorities and documented according to district protocols.
